'''John Michael Mallette''' (August 6, 1932 - August 21, 1995)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fold3.com/record/59903861-john-m-mallette-sr|title=John M Mallette Sr|publisher=Fold3|access-date=May 15, 2020}}</ref> was an American biologist, academic administrator and civic leader. He was a professor of biology at [[Tennessee State University]] and an administrator at the [[University of Tennessee at Nashville]]. He researched cholesterol, [[oral contraceptive]]s and [[cyclamate]]s. He is the namesake of John Mallette Drive in [[Nashville, Tennessee]].

==Early life==
Mallette was born on August 6, 1932, in Houston, Texas and attended St. Nicholas Elementary and High School there.<ref name="tennesseanritesset">{{cite news |first=Dwight|last=Lewis |title=Rites set for educator John Mallette Sr. |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/113226088/?terms=%22john%2Bmallette%22 |access-date=December 31, 2018 |work=The Tennessean |date=August 23, 1995|page=19|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|url-access=registration}}</ref> He graduated from [[Xavier University of Louisiana]] in 1954,<ref name="tennesseanmallettetoget">{{cite news |last1=Carmichael |first1=Alan |title=Mallette To Get UTN Post Today? |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/112031807/?terms=%22john%2Bmallette%22 |access-date=January 9, 2019 |work=The Tennessean |date=May 26, 1975|pages=1; 4|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|url-access=registration}}</ref> where he earned a bachelor's degree in chemistry. He served in the [[United States Army]] from 1954 to 1956 where he was medic and stationed in Germany.<ref name="tennesseanmallettetoget"/> He subsequently earned a master's degree from [[Texas Southern University]] in 1958 and a PhD from [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 1962, both in Biology.<ref name="tennesseanritesset"/>

==Academic career==
Mallette was a Biology professor at [[Tennessee State University]] from 1962 to 1974.<ref name="tennesseanritesset"/><ref name="tennesseannamedutnvice">{{cite news |title=Dr. Mallette Named UTN Vice Chancellor |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/112032795/?terms=%22john%2Bmallette%22 |access-date=January 9, 2019 |work=The Tennessean |date=May 27, 1975|page=10|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|url-access=registration}}</ref> He also taught part-time at the [[University of Tennessee at Nashville]] (UTN) from 1964 to 1974.<ref name="tennesseanritesset"/> In 1975, he resigned from TSU to serve as the vice chancellor of academic affairs at UTN for five years.<ref name="tennesseanritesset"/> He subsequently resumed his faculty position at TSU, where he taught for over three decades over the course of his career.<ref name="tennesseancouncilasked">{{cite news |last1=Wadhwani |first1=Anita |title=Council asked to rename one of Hydes Ferry streets |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/113571558 |access-date=December 31, 2018 |work=The Tennessean |date=April 18, 2001|pages=1B–2B|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|url-access=registration}}</ref>

===Research contributions===
Mallette did research on the effects of cholesterol on mice.<ref name="tennesseanmalettepresentspaper">{{cite news |title=Mallette Presents Paper |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/111658700/?terms=%22john%2Bmallette%22 |access-date=January 9, 2019 |work=The Tennessean |date=January 9, 1966|page=11|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|url-access=registration}}</ref> In particular, he studied the relationship between stress factors and their cholesterol rates.<ref name="tennesseanmallettetoget"/> Mallette also studied the side effects of [[oral contraceptive]]s.<ref name="tennesseanmallettetoget"/> According to ''The Tennessean'', he also did "pioneering research into the harmful effects of [[cyclamate]]s on animals which were later applied to humans."<ref name="tennesseanmallettetoget"/>

Mallette was the president of the Tennessee Academy of Science in 1975.<ref name="tennesseanmallettetoget"/>

==Civic activities==
Mallette was a member of the [[NAACP]], and he served on the boards of the [[United Negro College Fund]], the [[National Conference of Christians and Jews]], the [[United States Conference of Catholic Bishops]].<ref name="tennesseancouncilasked"/> He was honored as a Knight of the [[Order of St. Gregory the Great]] and a [[Knights of Peter Claver|Knight of Peter Claver]].<ref name="tennesseanritesset"/>

==Personal life, death and legacy==
Mallette married Pazette Berryman; they had a son and two daughters.<ref name="tennesseanritesset"/>

Mallette died on August 21, 1995, in Nashville.<ref name="tennesseanritesset"/> His funeral was held at the [[Church of the Assumption (Nashville, Tennessee)|Church of the Assumption]], and he was buried in the [[Greenwood Cemetery (Nashville, Tennessee)|Greenwood Cemetery]].<ref name="tennesseanritesset"/> In 2001, North Hydes Ferry in [[Bordeaux, Nashville|Bordeaux]], a neighborhood of Nashville, was renamed John Mallette Drive in his honor thanks to councilmember Melvin Black.<ref name="tennesseancouncilasked"/>
